newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition backs down on gold revaluation.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition backs down on gold revaluation.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition agreed Tuesday to back down on its controversial plan to revalue central bank assets after members of parliament from Kohl's party sharply criticised the proposal, a coalition source said.
Protests from conservative Christian Democrats forced the coalition to retreat from the plan to revalue central bank reserves, the source said.
"A solution is only possible with support of the Bundesbank," the coalition source told Reuters. "In face of the resistance from the Bundesbank, the revaluation for 1997 is no longer on the table."

Abandoning the plan to revalue the assets will mean that there is another 10 billion mark ($5.8 billion) hole in the 1997 budget, the official said. To fill that hole, the coalition was discussing privatisations, budget cuts and moderate tax increases.
Earlier, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said they were on the way to reaching an agreement on revaluing gold and currency reserves.
